content:
Maya: quick heads up 14 canary router is diverting ~4% of requests for org 'redwood-test' into the projectless fallback bucket, which is blowing through quotas
Sam: saw the quota alerts, thought it might be a scrape jitter. appreciate the flag
Jorge: incoming requests: are they api-keys or sa-tokens?
Maya: sampling shows API keys. introspector returns project_id=null even when X-Project-ID header is present
Nikki: that points at middleware ordering. the header->claim shim might be running after the routing decision
Erin: paste the minimal example and router trace?
Maya: example request:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/infer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_abc123" \
  -H "X-Project-ID: proj-42" \
  -H "X-Origin-Org: redwood-test" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Router snippet:
```
[1725009999.001] TRACE router: receive tx=tx-9a8b
[1725009999.002] TRACE auth:introspect => claims:{iss:api-key, project_id:null, org_id:"redwood-test"}
[1725009999.003] DECISION router: project_claim absent -> consult header X-Project-ID (found: proj-42) -> header-mapper returned null because it runs after rate-limit lookup
[1725009999.004] FALLBACK -> route to projectless-bucket(org-redwood-test)
```
Sam: yup ordering changed in rollout #4512 when we centralized header normalization into a separate filter. We intentionally kept it after rate-limit check to avoid cache-key explosion
Jorge: centralizing makes sense, but it didn't shim claims into the routing cache key for api-keys
Nikki: confirmed. the shim was moved post-rate-limit, which prevents router from seeing project claim during lookup
Erin: possible remediations:
- move shim before rate-limit lookup (simple, ups cache cardinality)
- update router to read raw headers as fallback before rate-limit decision (bigger change)
- special-case api-keys in the introspector to populate project from header (hacky)
Tony: prefer correctness on canary. revert shim order for canary and add a guard: only map X-Project-ID into claims when it matches an allowlist to limit cardinality
Maya: agree. targeted revert with allowlist plus rapid telemetry sounds good
Nikki: I'll draft a small patch: re-order shim and add config flag shim.allowlist_projects + guard to avoid wildcards
Erin: I'll add a dashboard tile: "projectless_route_pct" per-org and an alert for sustained >1% over 5m. Also add link to trace explorer on the tile
Sam: include a direct telemetry link to raw router traces in the alert body for faster debugging
Tony: can we canary the shim reorder to 10% first?
Maya: yes. 10% -> observe 30m -> 50% -> full. update runbook: revert to previous middleware order on rollback and note quota mitigation steps
deploy-bot: deploy request created: PR #5872 -> staging-canary (10%). CI: green :rocket:
Jorge: looping in infra to confirm rate-limit cache tolerates the small extra cardinality for 10%
Nikki: PR is up: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/5872. includes guard and a config toggle for allowlist
Maya: watching dashboard now. if projectless routes persist after reorder, we'll inspect the token introspection path itself
Sam: thanks folks :thumbsup:
Erin: dashboard & alert created: https://dashboards.redwood/c/projectless-routes
Tony: I'll write a short postmortem if we need one after canary
Maya: plan: ship canary, verify telemetry, then full rollout + add unit/integration test for header->claim mapping for api-keys
Sam: noted, will add QA ticket
